evaluationTargets.title: QIF v0.5.0 Living QIF Ledger release candidate
evaluationTargets.context: Self-evaluation of the QIF v0.5.0 package after adding the executable Living QIF Ledger for cross-package references, Quality Intent lifecycle, missed-intent records, and agent trial/outcome records.
evaluationTargets.operationalImpact: If the framework is incoherent, unverifiable, or misleading, downstream human or AI evaluations may produce unjustified quality verdicts.

qualityIntents.statement: QIF must present a coherent quality model where discovery lenses, evidence-type vocabulary, evidence, trust metadata, finding verification, confidence, verdicts, and governance have distinct responsibilities.
qualityIntents.lossBoundary: The framework must not collapse quality into checklist completion, activity counts, generic categories, or unreviewed AI findings.

qualityIntents.statement: QIF must remain executable through local schemas, examples, verifier logic, and retained negative fixtures.
qualityIntents.lossBoundary: A release candidate must not claim runtime readiness if its own schemas, examples, or verifier fixtures fail or drift.

qualityIntents.statement: QIF must be understandable and usable by AI agents without relying on hidden maintainer knowledge.
qualityIntents.lossBoundary: An AI agent must not need undocumented assumptions to author, evaluate, or challenge QIF artifacts.

qualityIntents.statement: QIF must be releasable without stale release artifacts, unpublished local-only assumptions, or missing trust and provenance evidence.
qualityIntents.lossBoundary: A public release must not omit updated release notes or publish unverifiable local/private residue.

qualityAspects.name: functional suitability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether QIF performs its intended representation and evaluation job.
discoveryQuestions: Can a real target be represented, evaluated, and governed with current QIF artifacts?
possibleLossBoundaries: QIF must not make quality verdicts impossible to explain.
antiPatterns: Treating the presence of entities as proof that the model works.

qualityAspects.name: auditability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether claims can be traced to artifacts and verifier results.
discoveryQuestions: Can every verdict cite retained evidence and an explicit verifier boundary?
possibleLossBoundaries: QIF must not present unchecked claims as audited truth.
antiPatterns: Equating a passing verifier with semantic correctness.

qualityAspects.name: maintainability
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether QIF can evolve without breaking retained contracts.
discoveryQuestions: Can new metadata be added without noisy rewrites or fixture drift?
possibleLossBoundaries: QIF changes must not silently weaken verifier coverage.
antiPatterns: Relying on manual memory to keep examples and schemas aligned.

qualityAspects.name: brand trust
qualityAspects.purpose: Discover whether public users can trust the release state and provenance of the framework.
discoveryQuestions: Would a user know what is verified, what is provisional, and what still needs release work?
possibleLossBoundaries: QIF must not publish a release that obscures what was actually verified.
antiPatterns: Treating local commit success as public release readiness.

evaluationPerspectives.rationale: Self-evaluation must check conceptual coherence and executable behavior.
QIF claims must be grounded in schemas, examples, tests, and runtime logs.
AI and human users need usable operating guidance and clear trust boundaries.

quantitativeEvidenceRecords.interpretationRule: The count is evidence of managed-project runtime integrity only; it is not quality itself.
quantitativeEvidenceRecords.knownLimitation: AOF structural verification does not prove QIF semantic truth.

automatedEvaluationDetails.notes: npm test passed with 8/8 positive package checks and 392/392 retained negative fixture checks for QIF v0.5.0.

qualityGateRules.title: Concept boundaries must remain explicit.
blockingConditions: No-Go if QIF treats aspects, metrics, activity counts, or AI findings as quality itself.

qualityGateRules.title: Executable baseline must pass local verification.
blockingConditions: No-Go if npm test fails or the retained fixture corpus drifts.

qualityGateRules.title: AI authoring guidance must be explicit enough for use without hidden assumptions.
blockingConditions: Pending if AI-facing usage guidance is absent or contradicts schema behavior.

qualityGateRules.title: Release readiness must include updated public artifacts and publication state.
blockingConditions: At most Conditional Go while release notes are missing or the evaluated commit is local-only.

intentVerdicts.residualRisk: Conceptual coherence is structurally documented, including evidence type vocabulary, but semantic fitness still needs pilot feedback.
Local verification is strong, but CI/public release verification has not been observed in this turn.
AI guidance exists, but usability by independent agents should be tested in a pilot.
Release notes and public residue scan are clean, but the evaluated commit has not been pushed, tagged, or released.

residualRisks: QIF v0.5.0 is structurally executable and release-packaged, but not yet publicly published.
Self-evaluation cannot prove semantic truth; it needs independent pilot review.
The evaluated state is local until pushed and tagged.

conditions.condition: Push the evaluated commit and tag the exact verified SHA when releasing.
conditions.monitoring: Confirm git status is clean, origin/main points at the released commit, and GitHub release v0.5.0 references the same tag.

qualityGateDecisions.rollbackPlan: If release packaging is found incomplete, do not tag; keep the local commit unpublished or publish a follow-up patch with corrected release artifacts.
qualityGateDecisions.monitoringPlan: After release, verify GitHub tag, release notes, npm test result, and absence of public residue.
qualityGateDecisions.customerImpactPlan: Notify early pilot users that verifier success proves structure and traceability only, not semantic quality truth.
qualityGateDecisions.decisionSummary: Conditional Go for QIF v0.5.0 release: qif-ledger retained fixture coverage is executable and traceable; qif-ledger retained fixture coverage remains a known follow-up.

governanceTriggers.reason: The model is executable and release-packaged enough for a Conditional Go, but the verified commit is still local-only until push, tag, and GitHub release complete.
governanceTriggers.requiredAction: Publish the exact evaluated commit and create the v0.5.0 tag and release before claiming public v0.5.0 release completion.

governanceTriggers.reason: Release-readiness evidence contains support (clean residue scan and release notes) and one remaining contradiction (local-only commit), so the release decision must stay conditional until publication is complete.
governanceTriggers.requiredAction: Resolve publication-state contradiction before recording a Go decision.

checks: confidence reproducibility from evidence and policy
governance trigger presence for release conditions
evidence type vocabulary declaration and usage
doesNotClaim: that fixture count is quality itself
semanticValidityRequires: pilot use by another AI or human evaluator

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Evidence produced by running local structural verifiers and retained fixture suites.
antiPatterns: Treating passing local checks as semantic truth.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Evidence produced by AOF managed-project runtime verification.
antiPatterns: Treating AOF structural verification as QIF semantic validation.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Evidence produced by reviewing public QIF documentation against implementation behavior.
antiPatterns: Treating documentation existence as proof of user comprehension.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Evidence produced by scanning public files for disallowed local or personal residue.
antiPatterns: Treating a clean string scan as proof of all publication safety.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Evidence produced by reviewing release notes, changelog, and release package artifacts.
antiPatterns: Treating a release note as proof that the release was published.

evidenceTypeVocabulary.purpose: Evidence produced by checking local and remote Git publication state.
antiPatterns: Treating a local commit as a published release.

evaluationTimingRules.title: Release candidate verification must happen before public release claim
triggerConditions: A public tag or GitHub Release will be created.
evaluationTimingRules.latestAllowedStage: before public release completion is claimed
antiPatterns: Publishing first and treating later verification as equivalent.
Using commit count or fixture count as quality itself.

evaluationTimingDecisions.decisionRationale: The release-readiness and executable-baseline intents require local verifier, AOF verification, documentation review, and public-readiness scan evidence before the public release is claimed.

evidenceRetentionPolicies.title: QIF release evidence retention policy
evidenceRetentionPolicies.retentionPeriod: Retain with the released repository history and release notes for the supported life of the release line.
evidenceRetentionPolicies.disposalRule: Do not dispose while the release tag, release notes, or related governance trigger remains active.
antiPatterns: Keeping only pass counts without retaining the artifact references needed to reconstruct the verdict.

qualityReports.title: QIF v0.5.0 self-evaluation quality report
qualityReports.reportPurpose: Summarize the self-evaluation gate decision without treating the report score as quality itself.
qualityReports.summary: QIF v0.5.0 is structurally executable and adds the Living QIF Ledger cross-package verifier surface; semantic validity still requires pilot feedback.

reportedScores.label: Self-evaluation confidence summary
reportedScores.calculationNote: This score reports the self-evaluation gate confidence and decomposes into the cited intent verdicts and their evidence.

sections.heading: Release readiness
sections.narrative: The report summarizes documentation, executable verifier behavior, AOF runtime evidence, public-readiness scan, release artifact review, and publication risk as cited by the self-evaluation gate verdicts.

limitations: The report summarizes referenced verdicts and evidence; it does not add independent semantic proof.
The report remains valid only for the evaluated commit and release package.
antiPatterns: Treating the report score as quality itself.
Publishing a report whose score cannot be decomposed into gate verdicts and evidence.
